signal: Nitro shipped version 26.1.1 with new Document Comparison for Mac and AI-based tools, and is now trusted by 67% of the Fortune 500

email.body1:
Garret, saw Nitro shipped 26.1.1 with Document Comparison and a wave of AI document tools, with 67% of the Fortune 500 already on board.

Global sales at that scale usually means more in-market accounts than the team can cover before reps ramp, and that is where pipeline leaks. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Nitro off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Garret, quick follow-up for Nitro.

Running global sales, you know new AI features spike demand across regions faster than headcount can absorb. Most teams don't know exactly how many meetings they need to hit the global number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Nitro needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Garret, last bit of proof for Nitro.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Nitro's reply rate likely compares to other global software teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Garret, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority for Nitro this quarter, no problem at all. Timing matters most right as you push new AI features globally, and I know that stretch is busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a global motion? I'll tailor it to Nitro either way.
